# Keymap

Every command's default key (UI-21). A key follows TrenchBroom's default where TrenchBroom binds the same action (MAP-20), named as its `ActionManager.cpp` names it at TrenchBroom/TrenchBroom@8f329f11e65e3d21b355a42bcae199cb3e4e0812; otherwise the choice is ours and the table says why. `secondary` is Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere. A key is changed in the keymap file (`docs/commands.md` lists the commands).

## Keys the map view takes itself

These act on what the map view holds, the selection it draws, its tool and its camera, so the view takes them itself while one of its panes has the keyboard, before a key taken anywhere. A texture key is taken while faces are picked for the UV editor.

| What it does | Keys | Follows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gives up the tool's work in hand, then the selection | `escape` | TrenchBroom's `Controls/Map view/Cancel` |
| Frames the selection in the 3D view | `secondary-u` | TrenchBroom's `Menu/View/Camera/Focus on Selection` |
| Selects everything shown | `secondary-a` | TrenchBroom's `Menu/Edit/Select All` |
| Selects what is not selected, and not what is | `secondary-alt-a` | TrenchBroom's `Menu/Edit/Invert Selection` |
| Selects what the selected brush covers in a 2D view, however deep | `secondary-shift-e` | TrenchBroom's `Menu/Edit/Select Tall` |
| Selects what is inside the selected brush | `secondary-e` | TrenchBroom's `Menu/Edit/Select Inside` |
| Selects what touches the selected brush | `secondary-t` | TrenchBroom's `Menu/Edit/Select Touching` |
| Groups the selection | `secondary-g` | TrenchBroom's `Menu/Edit/Group` |
| Ungroups the selected group | `secondary-shift-g` | TrenchBroom's `Menu/Edit/Ungroup` |
| Duplicates the selected group as a linked group | `secondary-shift-d` | TrenchBroom's `Menu/Edit/Create Linked Duplicate` |
| Hides the selection | `secondary-alt-i` | TrenchBroom's `Menu/View/Hide` |
| Hides everything but the selection | `secondary-i` | TrenchBroom's `Menu/View/Isolate` |
| Duplicates the selection | `secondary-d` | TrenchBroom's `Menu/Edit/Duplicate` |
| Deletes the selection | `delete`, `backspace` | TrenchBroom's `Menu/Edit/Delete` |

## Commands with no key

A command that answers a question is read by a panel, the agent or MCP. A command the window runs itself is a poll or a hand-over. A command that needs a value, a path, a name or a place, runs from the command line, which asks for each, or from the control in the window that has the value. A command run from a menu, or the palette, is used too seldom for a key.

| Command | Why | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checkpoint.list` | answers a question | Lists the open project's checkpoints, oldest first. |
| `checkpoint.restore` | needs a value | Puts every file of the open project back as a checkpoint holds it, removing the files made since and dropping unsaved edits, the open map's among them: the map is read again from its file, or closed when the file was made since. |
| `code.actions` | needs a value | Lists the quick fixes for the diagnostics at a place in a file: a missing builtin declared, a misspelled field corrected, an unused local removed, a missing precache added. |
| `code.fix` | needs a value | Applies a quick fix for the diagnostics at a place in a file, the first unless one is named by its index in code.actions' list; the file is not saved. |
| `commands.list` | answers a question | Lists every command with its id, summary and parameter schema. |
| `edit.accept` | needs a value | Accepts staged hunks: their lines stay in the editor's text, unsaved, once each hunk of their file is decided. |
| `edit.accept_next` | run by the window | Makes the next suggested edit, giving the next place that says the old name the new one, in the editor's text of its file; nothing is saved. Tab in the code editor runs it. |
| `edit.dismiss_next` | run by the window | Drops the suggested edits. Escape in the code editor runs it. |
| `edit.next` | answers a question | Answers the next edit the last one implies: after a field's, a function's or a global's name is typed over where it is first declared, the next place that still says the old name, and how many are left. |
| `edit.reject` | needs a value | Rejects staged hunks: the lines they replaced come back, byte for byte. |
| `edit.stage_change` | needs a value | Stages a change to several files as hunks to accept or reject one by one; the project is checked with them, and nothing is written to disk. |
| `edit.staged` | answers a question | Lists the staged hunks waiting to be accepted or rejected. |
| `engine.builtins` | answers a question | Lists an engine's builtins for a module kind, each with its number or engine name, QuakeC name, signature and extensions; the open project's engine and server QuakeC when none is named. |
| `engine.console` | needs a value | Runs a command in the running game's console and answers the lines it printed. |
| `engine.inspect` | needs a value | Reads the running game: the edicts in use, one edict's fields, every named global, or the call stack while stopped in a frame. |
| `engine.screenshot` | needs a value | Writes the frame the running game draws as a PNG, in the project's build/screenshots unless a path is given, and answers where and its size. |
| `file.close` | needs a value | Closes a file's tab, opening the tab beside it when it was         the open file; its unsaved text is kept. |
| `file.format` | needs a value | Formats a QuakeC file: each line indented with tabs to its depth, trailing white space removed. Only white space at the ends of lines changes, so it compiles to the same progs.dat; the file is not saved. |
| `file.inlay_hints` | needs a value | Lists a file's inlay hints: the name of the parameter each argument of a call is passed as. |
| `file.open` | needs a value | Opens a file in the editor, with the caret at a byte offset or at the start. |
| `file.read` | needs a value | Reads a file's current text: the editor's when it has unsaved changes, else what is on disk. |
| `file.replace_all` | needs a value | Replaces every match of a search in a file and saves it, as one undoable change; matching case, whole words and regular expressions as project.search. |
| `file.replace_range` | needs a value | Replaces a byte range of a file's text, in the editor's text; nothing is saved. An edit in an excerpt of the multibuffer. |
| `file.save` | needs a value | Writes a file's current text, as the editor has it, to disk. |
| `file.update` | needs a value | Takes the whole text of a file as an editor has it, unsaved, and checks the project again. |
| `files.changed` | needs a value | Takes files another program changed: the open map is read again when it has no unsaved edits, else kept for map.resolve_disk_change; changed QuakeC is read again with the entity definitions derived from it. |
| `git.blame` | needs a value | Says who last changed each line of a file, and in which commit. |
| `git.branches` | answers a question | Lists the repository's local branches, the checked-out one marked. |
| `git.commit` | needs a value | Commits what is staged with a message; the new commit's id. |
| `git.conflicts` | needs a value | Lists a file's merge conflicts: where each one's markers are. |
| `git.create_branch` | needs a value | Creates a branch at the current commit and checks it out, as git switch -c does. |
| `git.diff` | needs a value | Lists the hunks of a file's unstaged or staged changes. |
| `git.head_text` | needs a value | Gives a file's text at HEAD, which the editor marks its changes against; none for a file HEAD does not have. |
| `git.log` | needs a value | Lists the commits that changed a file, the newest first, following renames. |
| `git.resolve` | needs a value | Resolves one of a file's merge conflicts by keeping our side, theirs or both, and saves the file. |
| `git.stage` | needs a value | Stages a file, or one hunk of its unstaged changes. |
| `git.status` | answers a question | Lists the project repository's branch and changed files, staged and not, as git status does; none when the project is not in a git repository. |
| `git.switch` | needs a value | Checks out a branch, as git switch does, and reads the project's files again; refused while files have unsaved edits. |
| `git.unstage` | needs a value | Unstages a file, or one hunk of its staged changes. |
| `help.about` | run from a menu | Opens the About window: the app's name, version, copyright and license, and links to its site and its source. |
| `help.check_for_updates` | run from a menu | Looks for a later release of the app, with one request for the release feed, and says what it found: the version, and how to update with what installed this one. Nothing is downloaded or installed. |
| `help.report_issue` | run from a menu | Opens the page where an issue with the app is reported, in the browser. |
| `help.user_guide` | run from a menu | Opens the user guide on the website, in the browser. |
| `map.add_layer` | needs a value | Adds an empty layer to the open map, as TrenchBroom writes one. |
| `map.add_wad` | needs a value | Adds a WAD file to the open map's list in its world's `wad` or `_wad` key, by its path from the map's folder when it is under it, as TrenchBroom adds a WAD dropped on its window; one listed already is not listed again. |
| `map.apply_fix` | needs a value | Applies a quick fix `map.issues` gave, as one step with undo. |
| `map.backups` | answers a question | Lists the open map's backups in the autosave folder beside it, the newest first. |
| `map.balance` | answers a question | A balance sheet of the open map for each skill, 0 to 3, in single player, coop and deathmatch, read by spawning the map with the project's program: the monsters by class with the health their spawn functions give them, counted as the program counts total_monsters; the pickups that give weapons; the ammunition by kind with the damage id's weapons do with it (none for a mod's own); the health and armour given, each what touching the pickup gives a player; the secrets; and the damage over the monsters' health. Each for the whole map, each layer and group, and the entities in selection when given, each line with its entities. |
| `map.budget` | answers a question | How much of the target engine's limits the open map uses, and of id's: for each BSP lump, the face extent, edicts, precached models and sounds and light styles, what the map uses, the engine's limit with what the engine does past it, the share and whether it is past, near or within, worst first. The lumps come from the last compile while the map is unchanged; the edicts, precaches and light styles from the map spawned by the project's program on each skill. Limits past and near the target's join map.issues while the map, the target and the sources are the same. With answer "later" it answers null at once and spawns on its own thread; map.budget_found gives the answer. |
| `map.budget_found` | answers a question | Answers what map.budget found of the open map as it is now: the answer of a budget started with answer "later" once it is made, or the last answer while the map, the target and the sources have not changed since; null while one is being made, and when there is none. |
| `map.brush_chamfer` | needs a value | Chamfers an edge of a brush into one or more bevel faces, from a distance along each of its two faces (MAP-15.9). |
| `map.brush_clip` | needs a value | Clips a brush of the open map by the plane through three points, keeping the part behind it, in front of it, or both as two brushes. |
| `map.brush_create` | needs a value | Adds a box brush from two corners, snapped to the grid (16 units unless given), to the world or an entity of the open map, with a texture. |
| `map.brush_delete` | needs a value | Deletes a brush of an entity of the open map. |
| `map.brush_extrude` | needs a value | Moves a face of a brush along its normal by a distance snapped to the grid, out or in, its texture fixed in the world unless lock is free (MAP-15.3). |
| `map.brush_hollow` | needs a value | Hollows a brush into walls of a thickness: the brush becomes itself with the brush its walls enclose taken out (MAP-15.5). |
| `map.brush_hull` | needs a value | Adds to the world, or the entity given, the convex brush around points snapped to the grid, with a texture, as TrenchBroom's complex shape tool makes one. |
| `map.brush_intersect` | needs a value | Replaces two or more brushes of an entity with the solid all of them hold, which takes the first's place (MAP-15.6). |
| `map.brush_merge` | needs a value | Merges two or more brushes of an entity of the open map into their convex hull, which takes the first's place. |
| `map.brush_move` | needs a value | Moves brushes of an entity by an offset snapped to the grid (16 units unless given), their textures fixed in the world unless lock is free. |
| `map.brush_scale` | needs a value | Scales brushes of an entity by factors along x, y and z about a point, the middle of their bounds unless given, their textures fixed in the world unless lock is free (MAP-15.2). |
| `map.brush_shape` | needs a value | Adds a shape of brushes filling a box, its corners snapped to the grid: a cylinder (solid or hollow), cone, arch, UV or icosahedron spheroid, rock, scalable curve of 12, 24, 48 or 96 sides, or straight or spiral stairs whose default step a player climbs; to the world or an entity of the open map, with a texture. |
| `map.brush_shear` | needs a value | Shears brushes of an entity: each point moves along one axis by a factor times its distance from a point along another, their textures fixed in the world unless lock is free (MAP-15.2). |
| `map.brush_split_edge` | needs a value | Splits an edge of a brush by a new vertex at a point snapped to the grid, or a distance out from the edge's middle (MAP-15.8). |
| `map.brush_split_face` | needs a value | Splits a face of a brush by a new vertex in front of it, at a point snapped to the grid, or a distance out from the face's middle (MAP-15.8). |
| `map.brush_subtract` | needs a value | Subtracts a brush of the open map from every other brush of its entity, then deletes it: the brushes it overlapped become the parts outside it. |
| `map.brush_sweep` | needs a value | Sweeps a brush along a path of points snapped to the grid: the brush becomes one brush for each step, the hull of it at the step's two ends (MAP-15.4). |
| `map.brush_texture` | needs a value | Sets the texture, shift, rotation or scale of every face of brushes of an entity, keeping what is not given (MAP-12). |
| `map.brush_vertex` | needs a value | Moves a vertex of a brush of the open map to a point snapped to the grid; the brush becomes the convex hull of its vertices so moved. |
| `map.brush_vertices` | needs a value | Moves several vertices of a brush at once, each to a point snapped to the grid; the brush becomes the hull of its vertices so moved (MAP-15.7). |
| `map.brushes` | answers a question | Lists the brushes of an entity of the open map, the world's when none is named: each brush's place, which the map.brush_* tools take, the box around it and its textures; all of them, or those touching a box. The brush tools answer the places of the brushes they make, so this is for brushes whose places are not known: a map someone else built, or after a tool that changed how many brushes the entity has. |
| `map.build_passage` | needs a value | Builds a passage between two doorways of the open map that face each other along x or along y, 112 wide and 128 high, with stairs where their floors differ, a light, and a door when one is asked for. |
| `map.build_room` | needs a value | Builds one room of a shape of id's levels into the open map, sealed but for the doorways asked for, with its lights: a pillared hall, an eight-sided domed chamber, a hall around a pit crossed by bridges, a room on two levels, a courtyard, a cross of two aisles, a vaulted room, or an atrium with a balcony. Answers its doorways, for map.build_passage, and where things may stand. |
| `map.check` | needs a value | Checks a .map: what id's qbsp and ericw-tools read otherwise, and its entities against the project's server QuakeC as the engine reads them: unknown classnames and keys with the closest name, values their field cannot read, and targets and targetnames nothing matches. It reads the file alone, so it says a world that names no WAD is one as id's qbsp does; map.issues and map.find_leaks say whether a texture of the open map is missing. |
| `map.compare_with_disk` | answers a question | How the open map's file, changed by another program, differs from the map being edited, entity by entity. |
| `map.compile` | needs a value | Compiles the open map, as it is in the editor, or only a region of it, sealed, to a BSP beside it, with its portal and leak files, and reports whether it leaks and the textures its WADs lack. |
| `map.delete_entity` | needs a value | Deletes an entity of the open map; the world stays. |
| `map.duplicate_entity` | needs a value | Duplicates an entity of the open map, its keys and brushes, in place at the end of the map, and selects the copy; the world is not duplicated. A targetname ending in a number takes the next free number, and the keys the code fires entities by move on by as many. |
| `map.entities_removed_by_skill` | answers a question | The entities of the open map the game removes at a skill and in a kind of game (single, coop or deathmatch), found by spawning the map with the project's program: those the spawnflags rule out and those the QuakeC removes. |
| `map.export` | needs a value | Writes the open map to another .map without the layers marked to be left out of exports and the entities in them (TrenchBroom's Export). |
| `map.extract_linked` | needs a value | Moves entities of a linked group, and the same entities of every group linked to it, into new groups linked to each other (TrenchBroom's Extract Linked Groups). |
| `map.face_align` | needs a value | Carries one face's texture alignment onto other faces of the open map, so the texture continues across the line their planes share (MAP-13.8). |
| `map.face_uv` | needs a value | Fits, justifies, flips, resets, snaps or adjusts the texture of faces of the open map, at the size its WAD gives it (MAP-13). |
| `map.fire` | needs a value | Fires an entity of the open map as the game would, its use or its touch run in the simulation with the project's program, and answers what the QuakeC did about it in order: each use, touch and think the firing reached, each entity looked up by its targetname, removed or spawned, each centerprint and sound, and the fields written. Changes nothing: not the map, not a game that is playing it. |
| `map.flip` | needs a value | Mirrors entities and brushes along an axis through the middle of their box: brushes and point entities' origins, and their facing, as TrenchBroom's Flip. |
| `map.game_files` | answers a question | Lists the levels, models or sounds of the project's folder and the game's search path, each by the name the engine is given (a level as map takes it, a model by its path, a sound by its path under sound/) and where it is; the project's takes the game's place for a name both have. |
| `map.generate` | run from a menu | Makes a random playable level and opens it: rooms of several shapes on several floors joined by passages, stairs and doors, from a start to an exit, with loops, a balcony dropped from, locks (keys, a button, an arena), a secret room, lights, monsters and weapons, textured from the game's own levels, and no trap a player cannot leave: each level is compiled and checked as map.playability checks a map, with no jump, and a seed whose level fails gives way to the seeds after it. One seed gives one level. |
| `map.group` | needs a value | Puts entities and brushes of the world in a new group, in the layer or group the first is in, as TrenchBroom writes a group. |
| `map.hide` | needs a value | Hides entities of the open map in the editor until map.show_all (TrenchBroom's Hide Selection); the map is not changed. |
| `map.isolate` | needs a value | Hides every entity of the open map but these in the editor until map.show_all (TrenchBroom's Isolate Selection); the map is not changed. |
| `map.issues` | answers a question | Lists every issue of the open map, each with the entity or brush it is about and a quick fix where one exists: its format's, brushes with no volume, a missing player start, missing textures and, with a project open, its entities' against the server QuakeC. |
| `map.layers` | answers a question | The open map's TrenchBroom layers: each one's name, whether it is hidden, locked or left out of exports, and how many entities are in it. |
| `map.link_duplicate` | needs a value | Copies a group and its entities as a new group linked to it, so an edit in one is made in the other (TrenchBroom's Create Linked Duplicate). |
| `map.link_target` | needs a value | Points a key of an entity of the open map, one the code fires entities by such as target or killtarget, at another entity: the key takes the other's targetname, and the other its classname and the next free number as one when it has none. |
| `map.list_entities` | answers a question | The open map's rooms (TrenchBroom's named layers and groups, with their bounds) and its entities: each one's place, classname, origin, targetname and room, filtered by room or classname. |
| `map.logic_issues` | answers a question | Fires every entity of the open map that has targets, each in a copy of the spawned map, and lists what only running shows: a target with no use function, a chain that removes what it then fires, a chain that comes back to the same entity or stops the game, and an entity that fires its targets only at a firing the map cannot reach, such as a counter with too high a count. The issues join map.issues until the map or the code changes. |
| `map.list_textures` | answers a question | Lists the open map's textures: those of the WADs its world names, found in the project, beside the map or in the game, of the BSP it was opened from, and of the game's own levels, each once with where it comes from, its size and how many faces use it, and the names its faces use that nothing holds. |
| `map.lock` | needs a value | Locks entities of the open map against edits until map.unlock_all; the map is not changed. |
| `map.make_brush_entity` | needs a value | Makes brushes of the world a new brush entity of a class, such as func_door (TrenchBroom's Create Brush Entity). |
| `map.make_structural` | needs a value | Gives a brush entity's brushes back to the world, in the layer or group the entity was in, and removes the entity (TrenchBroom's Make Structural). |
| `map.move_entity` | needs a value | Moves an entity of the open map: a point entity's origin, a brush entity's brushes. |
| `map.move_to_layer_or_group` | needs a value | Moves an entity or a group of the open map into a layer or a group, or into the default layer given the world, as TrenchBroom writes it. |
| `map.new` | needs a value | Makes a new .map holding a world with the keys given, and opens it in the map view; a file that is there already is refused. |
| `map.open` | needs a value | Opens a .map in the map view, or a shipped .bsp's entities when the map has no .map source; nothing is selected. |
| `map.outline` | answers a question | The open map's outline: the default layer and each layer, their groups and linked groups, then their entities by classname and targetname, with brush counts; with filter, only what holds the text and what is around it. |
| `map.paste` | needs a value | Adds a .map's text to the open map, its world's brushes to the world and its other entities after the map's: where the text has them, or with the middle of their floor at a point on the grid. |
| `map.place_entity` | needs a value | Places a point entity of a classname at an origin in the open map, with the keys given, and selects it. |
| `map.place_prefab` | needs a value | Copies a prefab into the open map with its origin at a point on the grid: its world's brushes into the world, its other entities after the map's. |
| `map.play_from_here` | needs a value | Compiles the open map fast, with no vis and fast light, into the project's build, starts the game on it and puts the player's eye at a point, facing a way: the map view's camera (MAP-13), or with no eye the map's own player start. It answers where the player was put, the light there and the entities that stand in the dark; with start paused the game waits there with its monsters not yet awake, for a screenshot of the map as it was built. |
| `map.playability` | answers a question | Checks that the open map can be finished, as a player moves through it compiled: walking, falling, swimming, riding lifts and teleporters, opening doors with keys, buttons and triggers, and jumping (or with moves "generator", no jump). Answers whether an exit is reached from the player start, each key, weapon, item and secret never reached, each place from which the exit can no longer be reached, with a point inside it, and each entity whose class the check does not follow. Its findings join map.issues until the map changes. With answer "later" it answers null at once and searches on its own thread; map.playability_found gives the answer. |
| `map.playability_found` | answers a question | Answers what map.playability found of the open map as it is now: the answer of a search started with answer "later" once it is done, or the last answer while the map has not changed since; null while a search runs, and when there is none. |
| `map.portals` | answers a question | Reads the portal file the open map's last compile wrote beside it, each portal's points, to show where the map's leaves meet. |
| `map.prefabs` | answers a question | Lists the .map files in the project's prefabs folder. |
| `map.profiles` | answers a question | Lists the compile profiles: the built-in Full and Fast, then the project's own from compile-profiles.toml, each its name and its tasks. |
| `map.read_entity` | needs a value | An entity of the open map: its pairs, the keys its class reads with their types and defaults, and the map's targetnames for its target keys. |
| `map.remove_key` | needs a value | Removes every pair with a key from an entity of the open map. |
| `map.rename_key` | needs a value | Renames a key in every open .map, keeping each value and its formatting: what to run once the person confirms, after symbol.rename renames a field a map may name. Nothing is saved. |
| `map.replace_texture` | needs a value | Puts one texture in another's place on the faces of brushes, or of every brush of the map, keeping their alignment (TrenchBroom's Replace Material). |
| `map.resolve_disk_change` | needs a value | After another program changed the open map's file while it had unsaved edits: keep disk to read the file again, or mine to keep the edits and save them over it. |
| `map.restore_backup` | needs a value | Puts a backup of the open map in the editor in place of the map, unsaved, as an edit that undo takes back. |
| `map.rotate_entity` | needs a value | Turns a point entity of the open map about the vertical: its angle, or its angles' yaw. |
| `map.rotate_objects` | needs a value | Turns entities and brushes by degrees about the vertical through the middle of their box, counter-clockwise seen from above: brushes and point entities' origins and facing, as TrenchBroom's Rotate. |
| `map.save_prefab` | needs a value | Writes brushes of the world and whole entities of the open map as a prefab in the project's prefabs folder, around the middle of their floor. |
| `map.search` | needs a value | Finds the open map's objects as TrenchBroom's search does: text found in names, classnames, keys, values, textures, smart tags and layer and group names, ignoring case, or a query in its query language, which finds entities, groups, brushes, the contents of layers, or faces. |
| `map.set_flag` | needs a value | Sets or clears one spawnflag of an entity of the open map, and of the entities in also, in one step, keeping each entity's other flags. |
| `map.set_key` | needs a value | Sets a key of an entity of the open map, and of the entities in also with it in one step: its last occurrence keeps its place and formatting, a new key goes after the others. |
| `map.set_layer` | needs a value | Turns a layer of the open map hidden, locked or left out of exports on or off, written as TrenchBroom writes it. |
| `map.staged_hunks` | answers a question | Lists the open map's hunks waiting for review: for each, the entities it is in, and the keys and brushes it adds, changes or removes. |
| `map.summary` | answers a question | A map in short, to review it or compare it with others: the box around its brushes, its brush and entity counts, its entities counted by classname (monsters, lights, items, triggers), its textures counted by face, and its world's keys. The open map, or with a path a .map file read from the disk without opening it; with `most_textures`, only that many textures of the count it gives, which keeps it short when many maps are read. map.list_entities lists each entity; this counts them as the file has them, and map.balance counts what the game spawns on each skill. |
| `map.ungroup` | needs a value | Takes a group's entities and brushes out of it into the layer or group it is in, or the world's, and removes the group. |
| `map.unlink_group` | needs a value | Unlinks a group from the groups linked to it, which then change on their own (TrenchBroom's Separate Linked Groups). |
| `model.add_frames` | needs a value | Adds frames of another model of the same vertices to the end of a model's own, each by its name: QuakeC's $frame list gains the same names at its end. |
| `model.copy_from_game` | needs a value | Copies a model of the game, by its name there such as progs/soldier.mdl, into the project as a file of its own to change: a mod's file of the same name takes the game's place, and one of a new name is a new model. |
| `model.export_skin` | needs a value | Writes a skin of a model as a PNG, in the game's palette, to look at or to paint on and give back with model.set_skin. |
| `model.import` | needs a value | Makes a .mdl model in the project of a mesh in an .obj file (one pose), or an .iqe, .fbx, .md5mesh or .smd file (a frame for each frame of each animation, posed by its skeleton). A mesh with texture coordinates keeps them, on a PNG given as its skin or one colour; one without is laid out front and back, to export, paint and set. |
| `model.inspect` | answers a question | Reads a .mdl model: its skins, their size and the rows of the palette each is of, its vertices and triangles, the box it fills, and its frames by name in the order QuakeC numbers them, as a $frame line lists them. |
| `model.move` | needs a value | Moves a model against its origin, the point the entity's origin is at: its vertices keep their packed places and the header's origin moves. |
| `model.recolor` | needs a value | Recolours a skin of a model by rows of the palette: every pixel of a row becomes the same shade of another row, as the game recolours a player's shirt and trousers. |
| `model.remove_frames` | needs a value | Takes frames out of a model, each by its name. The frames after one taken out are numbered one less, so QuakeC's $frame list loses the same names. |
| `model.rename_frames` | needs a value | Renames frames of a model, each by its name. The game finds a frame by its number, so QuakeC's $frame names are its own: keep them in step. |
| `model.scale` | needs a value | Makes a model larger or smaller about its origin, on each axis: its vertices keep their packed places and the header's step and origin are scaled, so nothing is rounded again. The box QuakeC gives the entity (setsize) is its own to change. |
| `model.set_skin` | needs a value | Replaces a skin of a model with a PNG of the skin's size, each changed pixel matched to the nearest of the palette's colours that do not glow in the dark, or to a fullbright colour when it is exactly that colour. |
| `paths.open` | needs a value | Opens folders as projects, and files in the nearest project above each (a folder holding quakec.toml or progs.src): a .map or .bsp in the map editor, any other file in the editor. A file outside every project opens in the open project, or opens its folder when none is open. |
| `paths.take_opened` | run by the window | Takes what the last paths.open opened, once, or null: the desktop app shows it and comes to the front when another launch sent the paths. |
| `preview.breakpoint` | needs a value | Adds a breakpoint at a line of a file, or takes it away when there is one; set in the running game too and in each game that starts. A line with no statement is refused. |
| `preview.choose_game` | needs a value | Chooses the folder the preview reads the game from, in place, and says what it holds; a folder that cannot be played is not kept. |
| `preview.console` | needs a value | Runs a command in the running game's console. |
| `preview.dock` | needs a value | Docks the game's window beside the IDE's window, given where the IDE's window is and whether it has the focus. |
| `preview.game_files` | answers a question | Says what game data the preview plays from: the chosen folder, or the first install found, as found, shareware only, rerelease only or missing for the game the project is for, with the files it lacks. |
| `preview.pick` | needs a value | Selects the edict under a point of the game's window. A point with no edict under it answers none and leaves the selection as it was. |
| `preview.poll` | run by the window | Reads the running game's events: its state changes and console lines. |
| `preview.select` | needs a value | Selects an edict of the running game and reads its fields for the Properties panel. |
| `preview.set_field` | needs a value | Sets a field of the selected edict while the game is paused, the value read as the field's type. The game is given the value when it resumes, and reads the old one until then (`applied`: `on_resume`); each poll lists the fields waiting (`held`). |
| `preview.step_by` | needs a value | Steps the game stopped in a frame by a statement, into a call, over one or out to the caller. |
| `preview.unwatch` | needs a value | Takes a watch away. |
| `preview.watch` | needs a value | Adds a watch, an expression read each time the game stops in a frame. |
| `preview.watch_names` | answers a question | Lists what a watch may read where the game stopped: the locals, parameters and globals visible on that line, and the fields of self, each with its type. |
| `project.entities` | answers a question | Lists the entity classes the open project's server QuakeC defines, read from its spawn functions: each class's keys, defaults, spawnflags, comment, model and size; with fgd, also writes them as an FGD file for other map editors. |
| `project.files` | answers a question | Lists every source file the open project compiles, by path. |
| `project.info` | answers a question | Describes the open project: its directory and each module's kind, dialect, target engine and output. |
| `project.new` | needs a value | Makes a new project from a starter template, id's QuakeC 1.01 or the rerelease's, with quakec.toml, a sample test and the GPLv2 notices; it builds and plays at once. |
| `project.open` | needs a value | Opens the QuakeC project in a directory: its quakec.toml, or its progs.src and csprogs.src. |
| `project.reference` | answers a question | The reference to read before writing or debugging QuakeC or building a map, by topic: quakec (the language in short, how a mod runs, pitfalls); the dialect in full, with the mistakes a model makes in it: vanilla (id's QuakeC) when project.info says vanilla; when it says fteqcc, rerelease (what FTEQCC adds for id's VM), and fteqcc too (integers, pointers, classes) where the project's own code uses them; entities (what the engine calls, movetype and solid, the builtins by purpose, debugging); monsters, weapons, items and triggers (how each is written, from id's own, and every place a new one is added); models (what a model is, and how to recolour, scale and reframe one); maps; workflow (tests and scenarios). Written from id's QuakeC and the engine's specs; a mod's own code comes first where it differs. |
| `project.search` | needs a value | Finds every match of a text in the open project's files, unsaved edits included, by file, line and byte range; matching case, whole words only or as a regular expression. |
| `project.symbols` | answers a question | Lists the open project's global definitions, functions, globals and fields, each with where its name is first written; a query keeps those whose name contains it. |
| `project.take_checked` | run by the window | Takes the problems, symbols and highlighting the background check worked out for the latest edit, if it has finished; says whether anything changed. |
| `scenario.run` | needs a value | Builds the open project and plays a scenario file on it in the server simulation, answering whether each assertion held, with the values read, and writing its screenshots beside it. |
| `settings.get` | needs a value | Gives one setting's value and where it comes from. |
| `settings.list` | answers a question | Lists every setting with its default, its value and where the value comes from. |
| `settings.reset` | needs a value | Removes a setting from the user's or the project's settings file and writes the file. |
| `settings.set` | needs a value | Sets a setting in the user's or the project's settings file and writes the file. |
| `symbol.complete` | needs a value | Lists the names that may be written at a place. |
| `symbol.definition` | needs a value | Finds where the name at a place is defined. |
| `symbol.hover` | needs a value | Says what the name at a place is: its declaration and its comment. |
| `symbol.references` | needs a value | Finds every declaration and use of the name at a place, in every file. |
| `symbol.rename` | needs a value | Renames the name at a place everywhere it is written, in the editor's text of each file; nothing is saved. |
| `task.list` | answers a question | Lists the open project's tasks: the named command lines of its quakec.toml. |
| `task.run` | needs a value | Runs one of the open project's tasks in a new terminal tab, by the user's shell in the project directory. |
| `terminal.close` | needs a value | Closes a terminal tab, ending its process. |
| `terminal.poll` | run by the window | Takes what the terminal tabs have written and how their processes ended, without waiting; true when any tab changed. |
| `terminal.send` | needs a value | Writes a line to a terminal tab's shell. |
| `texture.import` | needs a value | Imports a PNG image as a texture: quantized to the game's palette with its mip levels, written into the project's own WAD in textures/, in place of a texture of the same name, and that WAD named in the open map's world. |
| `view.map_camera` | answers a question | Sets the map editor's camera: the 3D view's field of view, 50 to 150 degrees, how fast the mouse and keys move it, 0.1 to 10 times, and which way a vertical look and the wheel go. Settings not given are kept. |
| `view.map_grid` | needs a value | Sets the map editor's grid in units, a power of two from 0.125 to 256. |
| `view.map_grid_step` | needs a value | Halves or doubles the map editor's grid, held to 0.125 to 256 units. |
| `view.map_keep_view` | run by the window | Keeps a place and heading of the map editor's 3D view as a saved view. The window runs it for `view.map_save_view_1` to `_4`, with its camera. |
| `view.map_panes` | needs a value | Splits the map view: the 3D view alone, with a top view in its corner, or beside top, front and side views. |
| `view.map_shading` | needs a value | Draws the map view's 3D pane as the brushes' edges, as their textured faces, or lit by the last compile's lightmaps. |
| `view.move_panel` | needs a value | Moves a panel to another dock, where it shows, as Zed's status-bar menu moves one. |
| `view.pop_in_game` | run from a menu | Puts a popped-out game back in the Game tab, where it keeps running. |
| `view.pop_out_game` | run from a menu | Pops the game out of the Game tab into a window of its own, still run in the editor's process, so it keeps running; closing the window puts it back. A game in the preview host's own window stays there. |
| `view.resize_panel` | needs a value | Sets the width of the left or right panel, or the height of the bottom panel, in points. |
| `view.show_panel` | needs a value | Shows a panel in its dock, opening the dock; when the dock already shows it, hides the dock, as a click on Zed's status-bar button does, unless when_shown is keep. |
| `view.toggle_panel` | needs a value | Shows or hides a panel: Project and Entities on the left, Properties and the agent on the right, or Problems, Console and the debugger at the bottom. |
| `view.zoom` | needs a value | Draws the interface's text and icons larger or smaller, from 0.5 (50 percent) to 3 (300 percent); 1 is the actual size. |
| `vm.run` | needs a value | Builds the open project and calls one QuakeC function in the VM over a mock engine, with globals and the fields of a self edict set first, answering each global and field the call changed and any run error. |
